paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: you can bring the LORD your whole mess. David doesn't clean it up first. He says, "Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail," and he says it with aching bones, a distressed soul and a bed soaked with tears (Psalm 6:2-3, 6). The LORD never asks David to come back when he's feeling stronger. Being worn out is a perfectly good reason to pray.

Look at what David does with the waiting, too. He cries, "How long, O LORD, how long?" and he says it out loud, right to the LORD (Psalm 6:3). Then he asks the LORD to save him "because of Your loving devotion" (Psalm 6:4). David doesn't lean on how strong he is or how well he's behaved. He leans on who the LORD is, and that is a MUCH sturdier place to stand.

Then the song turns. David says, "The LORD has heard my cry for mercy; the LORD accepts my prayer" (Psalm 6:9). Nothing in the psalm says the pain has stopped yet, but David is sure he was heard. So when your own night is long, baker, keep praying, because you are talking to a LORD who hears. And I'll tell you what, that kind of hope is worth more than a whole warm batch of cookies.
